notes:
- Posters from btttr.cc, if you want them: Cards can now draw a rendered poster from btttr.cc - the art with the title and score set into it - instead of AniList's key visual. Choose it in Interface > Card design > Poster art. btttr addresses posters by IMDb id, so each title's id is looked up once and remembered; a title it does not carry, or a lookup that fails, keeps the AniList cover rather than an empty card.
- The whole app has a density setting: Interface > Layout has a Display density slider from 320 to 600 dpi, and the app now draws at 447 dpi by default instead of whatever the panel reports. Every length in the app is a dp, so the number decides how much fits: raise it for more on screen, lower it for larger cards, text and gaps. It applies to the whole app, including the page you set it on, and Reset density returns it to 447.
- The schedule reads like the library: Schedule rows are now the library's list row, larger: a poster big enough to recognise, a bold name, the air date as a pill and your progress under it, with more space between rows and between the airing and upcoming groups - so two shows no longer read as one card.
- Card design has its own page: The card-style picker now shares a sub-page with the rest of the card: how large the anime name is drawn, how large the score is, how big a card is in the grid, whether names are bold, and whether a name too long for its line scrolls instead of being cut. One preview at the top shows all of it at once, so a change lands on a card you are already looking at.
- One card design, everywhere: The size and weight you choose apply to every card in the app - the library grid, a profile's poster list and the sequel rows on Home - because they all draw the same card. A value written by an older build is brought back inside the slider's range instead of being drawn, and Reset card design returns everything to the shipped card.
- Card size decides how many fit: Compact, Standard and Roomy add or remove one cover from the row in every poster grid, and the poster stretches with it so a two-across card is a bigger picture rather than the same cover with a wider gap. List, Grouped and Table keep their single column, because a row is not a card.
- Previews show the page, not a diagram: The layout, library and sequel previews are now full page-shaped draws with real names, scores and progress instead of grey bars: the new Home opens with a greeting, its shortcut tiles say what they do, and the classic page shows its three counts. The library preview has the header every mode shares, plus the headings, columns and captions that tell the modes apart.
- Your own rating, on your own list: The library grid printed a name, a progress pill and nothing else, so what you gave a title was only visible after opening the entry. Every poster now carries the score you gave it, in the same star the list and table columns use, and the rating size on the Card design page scales it. This is AniList's own score for your entry, not the community average.
- Two switches for whose rating a card shows: Card design now asks which rating to print: yours on your list, and the profile owner's on somebody else's. Each is a switch, so you can see what you gave a title without turning every profile into a scoreboard, or the other way round. Off means the community average, which is what every card drew before - a title you never scored keeps that average either way, so no card loses its only number.
- Their score, in every list shape: On a profile's library the owner's own score is read from the list entry, so it is their verdict and not the app's guess, and it now appears in the grid, list, grouped and table shapes alike. AniList only returns those scores for a list it will show you, and an entry the owner never scored keeps the community average rather than an empty slot.
